subject: OpalWorks: replacement threat & proposed proof sprint to avoid replatform
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@opalworks.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@opalworks.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OpalWorks next steps after vendor brief

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the briefing yesterday. Internal review flagged two immediate asks from engineering and procurement: 1) a short-form throughput/latency bakeoff against EchoAI (their prospective replacement) focused on peak-hour p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens, and 2) clearer terms on burst capacity and guaranteed warm caches during holiday spikes.

We value the work Redwood has done but the board has asked us to validate both performance and unit economics before renewing the platform contract. Can you lay out a concrete plan (timeline, deliverables, and a firm POC window) so we can decide whether to proceed with Redwood or move forward with the competitor?

Also looped Priya from Ops — she'll own procurement timelines.

Best,
Samir
Head of Engineering
OpalWorks

[Attachment: opalworks-eval-asks.csv (text/csv) - 2KB]
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir Desai <samir@opalworks.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@opalworks.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWorks next steps after vendor brief

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. We can run a focused, three-week proof sprint that demonstrates:
- p95 latency at your typical payloads (50–250 tokens) under simulated peak-hour concurrency
- cost per 1M tokens across the model variants you care about (fp16 vs int8/quantized)
- a warm-cache / burst capacity run that simulates holiday bursts (x3 baseline throughput for 2 hrs)

High level plan:
Week 0 (prep): agreement on test harness, sample prompts, and traffic profile (you own the sample prompts; we provide default set)
Week 1: baseline runs + tuning (runtime kernel selection, batch sizing)
Week 2: competitive side-by-side (we test Redwood-optimized model variant vs EchoAI sample)
Week 3: final report + one-hour technical walkthrough + cost model and optional term amendment

We can commit to a dedicated reserved pool for the test to match your latency SLOs and pin a model build for the duration. To make this actionable we will provide: 1) a bench plan doc (attached), 2) a short SOW draft, and 3) a HubSpot link for scheduling signoff. If procurement needs a PO or credit offset to run the trials we can discuss a one-time evaluation credit.

Deliverables I will attach now — Karthik will follow up with the test harness details.

Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-bench-plan.pdf (application/pdf) - 120KB]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@opalworks.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.k@opalworks.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWorks next steps after vendor brief

Samir / Priya — looping in technical details so you can validate the bench is representative. A few clarifications we need from you to lock the harness:
- canonical traffic profile CSV (peak qps/minute, p95 request size) — the sample you sent looks like average traffic; please provide 95th percentile spikes
- list of target models (open weights) you want compared. If you want EchoAI included we'll need either their model binaries or a stable benchmark endpoint
- success criteria: retain or beat EchoAI on p95 latency AND be within 10% of cost per 1M tokens (or justify where lower latency warrants higher unit cost)

Technical notes:
- We'll run both fp16 and int8 variants; our runtime will attempt kernel selection and micro-batching optimized for your sequence length distribution.
- For the burst simulation we'll warm the KV cache and prepopulate common prefixes to reflect production behavior.

Proposed calendar: kickoff Fri 28 Aug (30 min), baseline runs Mon 31 Aug, side-by-side Wed 2 Sep, final readout Thu 10 Sep. If that timeline is tight, we can compress to two weeks but we'll need a signed SOW and a sandbox dataset.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: throughput-readme.txt (text/plain) - 4KB]
From: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@opalworks.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@opalworks.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@opalworks.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWorks next steps after vendor brief

Thanks — schedule looks reasonable. A few procurement constraints:
- OpalWorks requires a 60-day evaluation notice for any vendor credit or concession; for faster timelines we need a short MOU and a commitment to a decision checkpoint (no later than 30 days after final readout)
- We can accept a one-time evaluation credit up to $25k if Redwood can confirm in writing

On the technical side — Samir will provide the 95th percentile traffic CSV by EOD today. We do not have EchoAI binaries but will spin up their hosted endpoint for the side-by-side; Redwood, please ensure your harness can call an external endpoint.

Priya
VP, Platform Operations
OpalWorks
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir Desai <samir@opalworks.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.k@opalworks.com>, procurement@opalworks.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWorks next steps after vendor brief

Samir/Priya — quick update and actions to keep timelines tight:
1) We accept the evaluation credit constraint and confirm a $25k evaluation credit; I'll get legal to draft a short MOU and attach the SOW draft for signature.
2) Kickoff: Fri 28 Aug, 11:00 AM PT — calendar invite sent (HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/123-opalworks-kickoff). Agenda: test definitions, traffic profile, access and endpoints, success criteria.
3) Please upload the 95th percentile traffic CSV to the Drive folder (link below) before kickoff so Karthik can seed the harness.
4) As a show of good faith we will pre-allocate a small dedicated pool for the runs to ensure cache warmness; if results support a Multi-Region Dedicated recommendation we will outline a capacity uplift plan in the final report.

Deliverables attached: redwood-bench-plan.pdf and SOW-draft-opalworks-v2.docx. Please review and confirm procurement point of contact for DocuSign.

Looking forward — we'll aim for a tight, data-driven readout.

Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-bench-plan.pdf, SOW-draft-opalworks-v2.docx
